# 🟢 B-LIMB-1 CONFIRMED — all three fixtures classify correctly, 19/19 controls green.
# 🟢 B-LIMB-2 CONFIRMED — and on all three, not just one. The instrument earns its existence.
# 🔴 FIXTURE B IS THE ONE THAT CHANGES HOW THIS BASE MUST READ A GRANT, and it was the least
# expected. `os-taxonomy`'s payload is the UNMODIFIED, CORRECT, RECOGNISED stock ODbL text.
# Nothing about the FILE is unusual — no hand edit, no bespoke title, no README caveat. The
# scope limit is IN THE STOCK TEXT'S OWN PREAMBLE:
#     "the ODbL only governs the rights over the Database, and not the contents of the
#      Database individually. Licensors should use the ODbL together with another license
#      for the contents, if the contents have a single set of rights..."
# 🔵 So a licence can be perfectly valid, perfectly standard, correctly identified by every
# instrument on this base — and still leave the repository's actual payload UNGRANTED. Neither
# a fold (whole-text identity), a template digest, nor a README probe can see this; only
# reading what the text says it governs. A studio that ships a derivative of an ODbL corpus's
# CONTENTS on the strength of "licence: ODbL-1.0, permissive-ish" has no grant for the part it
# shipped.
# 🟢 `covers(payload, path)` IS THREE-VALUED, and that is deliberate. It returns None — not
# False — when the payload names subtrees and the queried path is not among them, because the
# answer is NOT STATED rather than refused. 🔵 This is a direct lesson from p381, which lost a
# finding by reading p351.classify()'s None ("a valid address") as "not an address". An
# undefined grant reported as False would read as a refusal and would be published as one.
# 🔴 THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN DECLARED LIMIT, pre-registered before it was built: these are three
# fixtures CHOSEN by the pass that wrote the classifier. 19 green controls show it handles the
# three known shapes; they establish NO BASE RATE for how common per-subtree grants are in the
# wild. The next pass with an execution lane should run it across the MIT tier's 884 read
# payloads and publish the DENOMINATOR.
# 🔴 AND THE LANE: p382 could not run this under `make hooks` — the execution lane is DENIED
# for cloned code in this sandbox (policy, not egress). The suite was authored and run 19/19
# green in the open lane (own-authored code, scratchpad) and is WIRED into HOOK_GATES as
# `gate-subtree-grant` so the first pass with a lane judges it. Roster now reads 45 gates,
# verified by `make -n hooks` expansion rather than by a run.
